$comment: THE ONE CANONICAL DECLARATION OF EVERY SQL SUITE IN THIS REPOSITORY.
scripts/run-platform-tests.sh derives its CANONICAL_GATE list from this file, and
scripts/verify-sql-suite-registry.mjs fails the gate when a suite file is undeclared, a declared
path has gone, a disposition is invalid, or a CANONICAL_GATE suite is not actually executed. There
is deliberately no second hand-maintained list: the duplicate entry Batch A found in the runner's
old array cannot exist here, because a JSON object cannot hold the same key twice.
CANONICAL_GATE   executed by the release gate on every run; its result is acceptance evidence
SPECIAL_PURPOSE  deliberately not in the gate -- declared manual, or dependent on another suite's
seed. Never counted as gate coverage
SUPERSEDED       another suite now guards the behaviour; the successor is named
RETIRED          the behaviour it guarded no longer exists
UNVERIFIED       not yet archaeologised. Declared so that it is not silent; NOT evidence of anything

Self-seeding and rolled back.

step17_legacy_retirement.reason: Convergence Step 17 (Identity/Auth Slice 10): the retirement slice's own acceptance is 'zero references in CI; full runner, clean boot and all browser suites green; production usage telemetry zero for 30 days before each drop', and measured against that NO DROP IS DUE -- every compatibility target still has live references. step16_governing_closure.reason: Convergence Step 16: the closure of the governing/competition relationships. Proves that a governing-body invitation is the CANONICAL one (registered capability, hashed token, single use, the organisation as its scope) and that there is no second invitation system; that a registered and an unregistered address are invited indistinguishably, which is what removed the account-existence oracle; that redemption is server-authored, bound to the invited identity, single-use and re-checks the ISSUER's standing at the organisation; that revoke and resend come from the canonical authority; that a body organiser can now read its own competition through RLS -- including the match verifications, which have no public fallback and were previously invisible to it -- and is notified when its clubs answer, which it was not; that a club can read which competitions it is in and who runs them while entry stays the organiser's act with no consent vocabulary invented; that affiliation and organising confer no club authority in either direction; the races Step 16 creates (two admins inviting one address, redemption versus revocation); and the boundaries it did not cross -- the organisation capability scope, the dispensation chain, club affiliation and protected person data.

step15_governing_product.reason: Convergence Step 15: the one RED change is a single added disjunct in internal.can_organise_competition -- the chokepoint all ten competition mutations reach through internal.require_edition_organiser -- so this proves the whole organiser matrix (right body, wrong body, viewer, Club Admin, Fixture Secretary, Safeguarding Officer, ordinary member, stranger), that the existing club and Site Admin organisers survived, that a body officer gains no authority over a club's own fixtures, and the three new writes: competition creation in the body's own rugby code and the canonical season, grant-by-email with no people-search surface, and revocation as a state change that is never your own. team_fixture_authority.reason: Team fixture operations: who may administer a team's fixtures, and how far that reaches. Proves that the shipped Coach bundle DOES grant team-scoped create/edit/cancel and request.create -- recorded as the product's actual behaviour rather than assumed away -- while never reaching a team the person is not attached to and never becoming club-wide authority; that a Club Admin's scoped DENY overrides the role bundle for one person on one team and takes nothing else with it; that a capability granted for one team is not authority over another for create, edit, cancel or request; that a fixture request is refused at source against a different age band or a senior side, BY THE CANONICAL RULE (internal.teams_can_play_fixture, asserted on the message so an unrelated check constraint cannot pass for it) while a request whose opponent is not yet known is still allowed; that club-wide authority is unchanged in a club context; and that the Planner, bulk import and bulk edit remain separate and are not even grantable at team scope.

mobile_fixture_authority.owner: Ovalball mobile client and fixture authority
mobile_fixture_authority.reason: M5: the authority the mobile Fixtures product consumes and cannot widen. Proves the four keys mobile asks for (fixture.fixture.create/edit/cancel, fixture.request.create) are team-scoped and delegable while the older short keys fixture.create/edit/cancel are NOT -- the distinction an interface built on the wrong pair would silently ignore every delegation over; that a role bundle is the default, an explicit team deny refuses one person on one team and takes nothing else with it, and an explicit team grant confers nothing on the club's other team; that team A's staff can neither edit nor cancel team B's fixture in the same club and hold no creation authority over it; that the Planner, Import, bulk edit and delete are not team-scoped capabilities at all and are refused even to a Club Admin asking at team scope, while the same Club Admin holds the Planner at club scope so the boundary is the scope rather than the person; that an ordinary member and a player mutate nothing; and that fixture-request compatibility is the canonical identities_can_play_fixture rule rather than a name match -- a far club's U12 is offered to our U12 and its U16 is not, a Rugby League side is refused for a Union one, an incompatible request is refused at insert time whatever a client offered, and the opponent picker refuses somebody who may not arrange fixtures rather than enumerating another club's sides to them. Self-seeding and rolled back.

mobile_message_attachments.owner: Ovalball mobile client and messaging attachments
mobile_message_attachments.reason: M4 completion: proves the attachment boundary is the platform's own -- the attachment and document-share RPCs take a fixture or a request and nothing else, so the mobile client's honest refusal on direct and club conversations is describing the platform rather than making a safeguarding decision on a handset, and a direct-conversation parameter appearing on either function fails this suite. Also proves the fixture-attachments storage path is authority rather than naming (an outsider knowing the exact path is refused, and a malformed or foreign-prefixed path is refused rather than erroring), that both RPCs refuse an outsider with 42501 and write nothing, that an image with no caption is a legitimate message while fixture_messages_content_present requires words alongside a non-image attachment -- which is why the mobile composer asks for a caption before it uploads a document -- and that a shared document is one reference to the club's own row, never a copy, and is not published to anybody outside the conversation. Self-seeding and rolled back; no persistent review identity, club, team, fixture or document is touched.

mobile_message_authority.reason: The authority the mobile Messages product inherits and cannot widen. The app reads through the same RPCs and RLS the website uses and sends by the same insert, so what is proved here is the SERVER's refusals: a conversation id is not a permission (the deep-link case), a forged sender column is refused, an outsider cannot rewrite a message, the inbox reader never lists somebody else's conversation, and candidate discovery is a per-caller function rather than a readable table. If the server refuses these, no client can perform them -- including a modified one.

availability_one_product.owner: Ovalball availability -- Match Centre, Training Centre, both clients
availability_one_product.reason: M6: availability is ONE product, and this proves the fixture half and the training half answer alike for the same person under the same policy. The archaeology that preceded the native Match Centre found three asymmetries, all of which would otherwise have been worked around in React Native. A cancelled FIXTURE now refuses an answer, as a cancelled SESSION always has -- the rule previously existed only in the web Match Centre resolver, so any other caller could record an answer to a match that is not happening. A fixture whose orientation is TBD or Not Applicable is answerable: the writer used to locate the fixture's teams through the generated home_team_id/away_team_id columns, which are NULL for both of those, so a legitimate answer was refused as 'this player is not associated with a team involved in this fixture' while the page offered three buttons. A Mini-Rugby scheduling-group fixture is answerable, including for a child on a partner team inside the group that does not own the fixture -- the writer knew nothing about groups and refused every one of them. It also proves the two readers, get_my_players_for_fixture and get_my_players_for_training_session, return an identical column set and each return only the caller's own family, with can_respond and denial_reason inline so neither client draws a control the write would refuse; that a cancelled event still LISTS the child, so a parent can see what was answered before it was called off; that the safeguarding rule is unchanged and still the database's -- guardian always, a 17-year-old with recorded guardian_player_permissions consent yes, a 16-year-old without it no, for both the reader and the write; and that there is one vocabulary of states, so 'MAYBE' and 'AWAITING' are refused and AWAITING remains the ABSENCE of a row. Proved to bite: with the pre-fix writer restored, A4, A5, B2, B3, B4 and C3 fail. Self-seeding and rolled back; no persistent review identity, club, team, fixture or session is touched.

participant_route_authority.owner: Ovalball participant routing -- Match Centre, Training Centre, the canonical fixture address
participant_route_authority.reason: P3: a participant never reaches administration, and never reaches another family. The defect this suite was written for is that `/fixtures/<id>` is the canonical address for one physical fixture on both clients -- what the website routes to, what notificationHref emits for every fixture notification, what a shared link carries and what the app restores after being killed -- and the mobile client had made it the FIXTURE CONSOLE, so every canonical way into a fixture put a parent in fixture administration. The fix is a route that asks the SERVER which surface to draw, which means the whole boundary now rests on the answers pinned down here. It proves: the route decision itself, because get_match_centre_capabilities.can_manage_fixture is false for a guardian on their own child's match and for a 16-year-old on their own, while remaining TRUE for a club admin on their own club's fixture so that legitimate operations are not collateral damage; that changing the id in the URL buys nothing, because another family's fixture grants a guardian no capability of any kind and get_my_players_for_fixture returns nobody for it, while their own child's match still works -- the half a blunt fix would have broken; that administration is refused at the WRITE and not merely left undrawn, for cancelling a fixture and cancelling a training session; that the Training Centre's own can_manage and can_view_register are false, which is what makes every editable row on that screen absent; and that opposition is informational rather than relational -- a guardian gets no opposition contacts and no opposition person among the people they may message, while the opponent's NAME on their own fixture stays perfectly visible. Self-seeding and rolled back, which matters more than usual here: the persistent review world contains no fixture outside any UAT family, so this boundary can only be proved against data a test owns. P4 extended it to the Training Centre in full: a guardian sees their own child on their own child's session and NOBODY on a session belonging to another family's side, whose card reader refuses them outright; every administrative write is refused directly as a typed URL would have called it -- moving the day, the start time, the ground, the session plan, and cancelling -- while answering for their own child is allowed, which is the participant half the boundary must not break, and answering for another family's child is refused. A 16-year-old player is a participant at training too. And a club admin may still actually rewrite the session plan, so the staff half is proved not to be collateral damage.

prerequisite_defect.finding: These suites end with `rollback;`, so a suite declared to run AFTER one of them finds nothing left behind. Every SPECIAL_PURPOSE suite whose prerequisites name one of them therefore CANNOT be run by its own documented procedure.
prerequisite_defect.consequence: Such a suite is not gate coverage and is not currently runnable coverage either. It must never be described as passing.
